titleEn: Why does the same perfume smell different on different people? ‘Skin chemistry’ explained
titleZh: 为什么同一款香水在不同人身上的气味不同？解读“皮肤化学”
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Have you ever sprayed a perfume in a department store on a paper strip and loved the smell, but it didn’t perform the same when you sprayed it on your skin? It’s a common experience.
paragraphs.zh: 你是否有过这样的经历：在百货商店把香水喷在试香纸上时很喜欢它的气味，可喷到自己的皮肤上后，效果却不一样？这种情况很常见。

paragraphs.en: It all has to do with how the molecules in the perfume evaporate and interact with your skin. That chemistry also explains why the same perfume may smell amazing on you, but on someone else it can smell completely different, and sometimes not nearly as pleasant.
paragraphs.zh: 这完全取决于香水中的分子如何蒸发，以及它们如何与皮肤相互作用。这种化学过程也解释了为什么同一款香水在你身上可能香气迷人，在别人身上却可能呈现出截然不同的气味，有时甚至没那么好闻。

paragraphs.en: That’s because each of us has different “skin chemistry”. As a result, perfumes will behave differently, and the smell our noses detect will vary.
paragraphs.zh: 这是因为每个人的“皮肤化学特性”都不同。因此，香水的表现会有所差异，我们的鼻子闻到的气味也会变化。

paragraphs.en: To understand why and how this happens, first we need to look at what is a perfume, chemically speaking.
paragraphs.zh: 要理解为什么会发生这种现象，以及它是如何发生的，首先需要从化学角度了解香水究竟是什么。

paragraphs.en: What’s in a perfume?
paragraphs.zh: 香水里有什么？

paragraphs.en: Simply put, a perfume is a mixture of various fragrance molecules, typically dissolved in alcohol. Perfumers carefully combine these ingredients into what are known as “top”, “middle” and “base” notes.
paragraphs.zh: 简单来说，香水是多种香气分子的混合物，通常溶解在酒精中。调香师会精心组合这些成分，形成所谓的“前调”“中调”和“后调”。

paragraphs.en: Top notes, such as citrus compounds like limonene, are highly volatile, will evaporate quickly, and not stay on the skin for long.
paragraphs.zh: 前调中的分子，例如柠檬烯等柑橘类化合物，挥发性很强，会迅速蒸发，在皮肤上停留的时间不长。

paragraphs.en: Middle notes, often floral or fruity molecules, emerge after the top notes fade because they’re less volatile and stick around for longer.
paragraphs.zh: 中调通常由花香或果香分子构成，在前调淡去后显现，因为这些分子的挥发性较低，能够持续更长时间。

paragraphs.en: Base notes, including musks, woods and resins, are the heaviest or largest molecules, so they evaporate more slowly and will linger the longest.
paragraphs.zh: 后调包括麝香、木香和树脂等，所含分子最重或最大，因此蒸发得更慢，留香时间也最长。

paragraphs.en: When a perfume is sprayed onto paper, the fragrance molecules evaporate (change from liquid to gas) in a relatively predictable way. Their ability to escape into the air is mainly determined by intermolecular forces – interactions between molecules.
paragraphs.zh: 把香水喷在纸上时，香气分子会以相对可预测的方式蒸发，也就是从液态变成气态。它们进入空气的能力，主要由分子间作用力决定，即分子之间的相互作用。

paragraphs.en: The stronger those forces are, the harder it is for a molecule to break away and change from liquid to gas. Molecule size and shape also play a role here. So, the top notes evaporate first because they’re small and have weak intermolecular forces, while base notes are the opposite.
paragraphs.zh: 这些作用力越强，分子就越难脱离并从液态变成气态。分子的大小和形状也会产生影响。因此，前调最先蒸发，因为它们的分子较小、分子间作用力较弱；后调则恰好相反。

paragraphs.en: Knowing all this about the molecules is what lets perfumers create fragrances that will release their notes fairly predictably.
paragraphs.zh: 了解分子的这些特性后，调香师就能调配出香调释放过程相对可预测的香水。

paragraphs.en: But it gets more complicated once fragrance hits the skin.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，一旦香水接触皮肤，情况就会变得更加复杂。

paragraphs.en: How skin chemistry enters the picture
paragraphs.zh: 皮肤化学特性如何产生影响

paragraphs.en: While a paper tester strip is a fairly neutral surface, we have various molecules on the skin. These interact with the perfume and can not only change the order of the molecules being released, but also alter or mask the resulting scent.
paragraphs.zh: 试香纸条的表面相对中性，而皮肤上存在各种分子。它们会与香水相互作用，不仅可能改变香气分子的释放顺序，还可能改变或掩盖最终呈现的气味。

paragraphs.en: The main skin factors that will influence the scent of perfume are:
paragraphs.zh: 影响香水气味的主要皮肤因素包括：

paragraphs.en: moisture content and oiliness
paragraphs.zh: 含水量和油脂程度

paragraphs.en: temperature
paragraphs.zh: 温度

paragraphs.en: pH level
paragraphs.zh: pH 值

paragraphs.en: microbiome.
paragraphs.zh: 微生物群。

paragraphs.en: Moisture and oiliness
paragraphs.zh: 含水量和油脂程度

paragraphs.en: Hydration is one of the main factors. Dry skin tends to absorb heavier or larger fragrance molecules more readily, while moist or oily skin provides a better surface for fragrance molecules to sit on and evaporate gradually.
paragraphs.zh: 皮肤的水分状态是主要因素之一。干燥的皮肤往往更容易吸收较重或较大的香气分子；湿润或油性皮肤则为香气分子提供了更适合停留并逐渐蒸发的表面。

paragraphs.en: This often improves how long the perfume lasts and its projection – how much others around you can smell it. This is why the same perfume could last all day on one person, but only for a couple of hours on another.
paragraphs.zh: 这通常会延长留香时间，并增强扩香程度，也就是周围的人能够闻到香气的程度。这也解释了为什么同一款香水在一个人身上能持续一整天，在另一个人身上却只能维持几个小时。

paragraphs.en: Temperature
paragraphs.zh: 温度

paragraphs.en: Warmer skin increases evaporation, causing perfumes to develop more quickly and sometimes smell stronger. A person with naturally warmer skin may experience top notes disappearing much faster. Base notes may become noticeable within minutes rather than an hour. This can make it seem as though the perfume “skips” the top notes.
paragraphs.zh: 较高的皮肤温度会加快蒸发，使香水的香调变化更快，有时闻起来也更浓。天生皮肤温度较高的人，可能会发现前调消失得快得多。后调可能在几分钟内就显现，而不是一小时后才出现，让人感觉香水仿佛“跳过”了前调。

paragraphs.en: pH level
paragraphs.zh: pH 值

paragraphs.en: The natural acidity of the skin, often referred to as skin pH, may also subtly influence fragrance performance. Human skin is slightly acidic, typically around pH 4.5 to 5.5.
paragraphs.zh: 皮肤天然的酸碱性，通常称为皮肤 pH 值，也可能微妙地影响香水的表现。人的皮肤呈弱酸性，pH 值通常约为 4.5 至 5.5。

paragraphs.en: While most fragrance ingredients remain stable within this range, subtle pH changes could cause fragrance ingredients to react differently. As a result some floral notes may weaken, some musks may become more prominent, some citrus notes may smell sharper or disappear rapidly.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然大多数香水成分在这一范围内能够保持稳定，但细微的 pH 变化仍可能让它们发生不同的反应。因此，一些花香可能减弱，一些麝香可能更突出，而某些柑橘香可能变得更尖锐，或迅速消失。

paragraphs.en: Skin microbiome
paragraphs.zh: 皮肤微生物群

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most fascinating factor is our skin microbiome. Our skin is home to billions of microorganisms, including bacteria and fungi. These microbes interact with compounds found in sweat and skin oils, producing volatile organic compounds that contribute to each person’s unique scent profile.
paragraphs.zh: 或许最有趣的因素是皮肤微生物群。皮肤上生活着数十亿微生物，包括细菌和真菌。这些微生物会与汗液和皮脂中的化合物相互作用，产生挥发性有机化合物，共同塑造每个人独特的气味特征。

paragraphs.en: The microbes can also metabolise fragrance molecules. This can produce new odours, enhance some notes, or suppress others. It’s another reason why a fragrance could smell wonderful on one person and unpleasant on another.
paragraphs.zh: 微生物还可以代谢香气分子。这可能产生新的气味、增强某些香调，或抑制其他香调。这也是为什么一种香水在某个人身上很好闻，在另一个人身上却可能不好闻。

paragraphs.en: Perfumes can be fickle
paragraphs.zh: 香水的表现可能变化不定

paragraphs.en: All this means that when you apply a perfume, it’s not interacting with a neutral surface, like a piece of paper. It’s combining with your own unique chemical background. A floral fragrance that smells fresh and rosy on one person may seem sharper, sweeter or even slightly sour on another, because it’s blending with different molecules on that person’s skin.
paragraphs.zh: 以上意味着，当你使用香水时，它接触的并非纸张那样相对中性的表面，而是会与你独特的化学环境融合。某种花香在一个人身上闻起来清新、带有玫瑰香，在另一个人身上却可能更尖锐、更甜，甚至略带酸味，因为它与那个人皮肤上的不同分子混合在了一起。

paragraphs.en: Even the same perfume on the same person can smell slightly different from one day to the next. Changes in hydration, hormone levels, diet (spicy or garlicky foods can make you smell differently), ambient temperature and skin condition can all affect fragrance performance.
paragraphs.zh: 即便是同一款香水，在同一个人身上，不同日子的气味也可能略有差异。水分状态、激素水平、饮食（辛辣或含大蒜的食物可能改变体味）、环境温度以及皮肤状况的变化，都可能影响香水的表现。

paragraphs.en: It pays to keep all this in mind when buying and using fragrances.
paragraphs.zh: 购买和使用香水时，把这些因素记在心里会很有帮助。

paragraphs.en: First, never judge a fragrance solely on a paper test strip. They’re good for a first impression, but can’t predict how a perfume will behave on your skin. Always test a fragrance on your wrist and wear it for several hours before deciding whether to buy it.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，不要只根据试香纸判断一款香水。试香纸适合形成第一印象，却无法预测香水在皮肤上的表现。决定购买之前，最好在手腕上试喷，并让它停留几个小时。

paragraphs.en: Second, don’t be disappointed if a perfume smells different on you than on paper or on your friend’s wrist. Biologically we’re all unique and you might have better luck with a different fragrance.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，如果香水在你身上的气味与试香纸或朋友手腕上的不同，不必失望。每个人在生物学上都是独特的，另一款香水也许会更适合你。

paragraphs.en: Finally, if you want a fragrance to last longer, applying an unscented lotion before spraying can often help – it will make the perfume evaporate slower.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，如果希望香味持续更久，在喷香水之前涂抹无香型乳液往往会有所帮助，因为这样能让香水蒸发得慢一些。
